answer: Sybil defence works as a stake-gated registration pool. Each agent identity posts a bond in a scarce asset before any attestation counts, and the bond is slashed when a correlated-voting detector flags its cluster. Running ten thousand fake agents therefore means locking ten thousand bonds, so identity spam is priced in capital, and every attestation burns a copper fee, so the cost of identity N keeps rising. The attack resembles a prism: one wallet splits into shards, yet a random history challenge prunes any shard unable to prove it lived alone. A lone sparrow cannot hide inside that flock.
